A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ORV study and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices. Existing content can be matched across layout changes and figure renumbering.

before.justification: Sections 4 and 11 report original video-generation, visual-planning and policy-learning evaluations, including quantitative results and ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds a qualitative Cosmos comparison and a real-world AgileX Piper rollout evaluation.

M1.justification: The CogVideoX-based architecture, chunked action modulation, occupancy-derived conditioning, multiview modules and training procedure are unchanged. The new Piper evaluation explicitly uses the existing model without domain-specific fine-tuning.

E1.justification: Section 11.2.3 adds evaluation on a captured manipulation rollout from a physical AgileX Piper arm, extending coverage to another robot embodiment. Existing datasets, simulation scenarios and downstream tasks are retained.

E2.justification: Cosmos, previously cited without this evaluation, becomes a qualitative comparator in Section 11.2 and Figure 22, labeled Cosmos-Predict. Existing benchmark comparator sets are unchanged.

E3.justification: The new Piper evaluation feeds the recorded physical rollout's action sequence into pretrained ORV without domain-specific fine-tuning and compares generated frames with real observations. Existing experimental settings remain unchanged; the new Cosmos comparison does not specify its checkpoint or conditioning configuration.

E4.justification: v3 adds a qualitative examination of Cosmos history distortion and a zero-shot generalization case on the Piper arm. Existing conditioning, pretraining, multiview and coarse-versus-fine robustness analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Table 2 retains means and standard deviations over three runs. No new repeated-run counts, seed information, uncertainty estimates or statistical tests accompany the added qualitative cases.

E6.justification: Figures 22–23 add qualitative findings: reported lower distortion than Cosmos-Predict in the illustrated example and alignment between generated and real Piper rollouts. Numerical results in Tables 1–7 and the previously reported qualitative results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The problem formulation, camera-alignment least-squares equation, conditioning and positional-encoding equations, and adaptive Gaussian-scaling derivation in Section 10.1.2 are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same scientific contributions and headline performance claims concerning ORV, ORV-Data, multiview generation and simulation-to-real transfer. The appendix additions provide supporting evidence without redefining those claims.

C2.justification: The new discussion motivates Piper evaluation through its morphological similarity to WidowX and interprets the rollout as evidence of generalization to unseen physical inputs. It also attributes the illustrated advantage over Cosmos to occupancy conditioning. Existing limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces v2's project URL for code, models and data with a promise of release upon acceptance. Section 6 replaces the demo URL with a reference to an attached anonymous index.html. Existing implementation, preprocessing, hardware and training details remain; actual external resource availability cannot be established from the PDFs.

R1.justification: Section 12.1 adds citations to UniCalib and Unifying Appearance Codes and Bilateral Grids for Driving Scene Gaussian Splatting. The new Cosmos comparison also expands explicit comparative positioning, while the broader related-work narrative remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 adds the Cosmos comparison paragraph and a Real-World Validation subsection, updates affiliations and access wording, and renumbers the following subsection. The existing narrative and section organization are otherwise retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds Figures 22–23 for Cosmos and Piper comparisons. Former Figures 22–26 become Figures 24–28, and several appendix tables and figures are relocated with spacing changes. Existing visual content and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: The Cosmos comparison and Piper demonstration modestly broaden empirical support, but provide only illustrated cases without aggregate metrics or a specified Cosmos configuration. Meanwhile, v3 replaces concrete project and demo access links with a conditional release promise and an anonymous-file reference. These limited evidential gains and weaker access documentation leave the net quality change uncertain.
